text:
alex: Starting a quick runbook thread for the new AP-south3 kubeadm cluster with A100s. Goal: fast, repeatable priming so platform team can hand this off to oncall and infra-custops.

maya: high level checklist please — I want to kick the nodepool warmup tomorrow morning.

alex: top-level steps: bootstrap control plane -> install CNI -> GPU driver + device-plugin -> base addons (coredns, metrics-server, kube-proxy) -> autoscaler config + taints/labels -> smoke validation -> handoff doc.

jin: small note: AP-south3 NICs have MTU 9000 by default, so ensure calico/cilium MTU matches, otherwise pod networking flakiness.

alex: good call. we'll set MTU=9000 in the CNI daemonset config. also using kubeadm with --pod-network-cidr=10.244.0.0/16 for simplicity.

maya: what about kubelet flags for GPU nodes? we used --feature-gates=DevicePlugins=true previously.

alex: kubelet should include device plugin enabled, and we need to set kube-reserved for GPU nodes: e.g., --kube-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=1Gi,ephemeral-storage=1Gi. Also system-reserved. Keeps scheduling stable under pressure.

jin: driver install approach? node-init daemonset vs pre-baked AMI?

alex: for this region we'll use pre-baked AMI with NVIDIA drivers baked to speed provisioning. But still install DCGM exporter + nvidia-device-plugin as daemonsets so upgrades are simpler.

maya: can you paste the device-plugin manifest snippet?

alex: sure, will drop the minimal snippet we'll use in the repo: ```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
        operator: "Exists"
      containers:
      - name: nvidia-device-plugin-ctr
        image: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: "100m"
```

jin: LGTM. Ensure node labels: "gpu=yes", "instance_type=A100" and taint: "gpu=true:NoSchedule" so non-GPU workloads don't land there.

alex: doing that in the nodepool provisioner. We'll also add a lightweight admission webhook to reject unsized pods on GPU nodes (no requests/limits) — prevents scheduler surprises.

maya: nets/security: we need firewall rules to allow node <-> controlplane on 10250, 30000-32767 for NodePort egress, and 2379-2380 for etcd in case we expand. Put those in the runbook.

alex: added. Also TLS bootstrap for kubelet and explicit kubeadm token rotation steps in the doc.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: PR: infra/ap-south3/kubeadm-priming. Link: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/512

maya: smoke tests I want: 1) small echo pod to verify DNS 2) gpu-burn container using one GPU 3) multireplica nginx to verify NodePort egress.

alex: planned smoke manifests: 
- dns-test: busybox nslookup kubernetes.default
- gpu-test: nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi inside container, run a small cudamat op
- network-test: curl to external endpoint from cluster to verify egress and MTU

jin: add cost note: pre-baked A100 nodes are expensive; enable scale-to-zero for nodepool spike workloads and autoscaler with ephemeral spot fallback policy. Document expected baseline RPS versus GPU hours we budget: baseline dev usage ~0.5 GPU-hours/day, warmup stress ~6 GPU-hours/day.

alex: will add autoscaler config snippet and suggested spot fallback settings. Also note for Dedicated customers we flip off spot fallback and require capacity reservations.

maya: how do we validate device-plugin actually exposes GPUs? command: `kubectl describe node <gpu-node>` shows Allocatable nvidia.com/gpu=1, and `kubectl get pods -o=wide` shows the daemonset on each node.

alex: also run: `kubectl run --rm -i --tty gpu-check --image=nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1' -- bash -c "nvidia-smi && python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())'"`

jin: nice. Add alerting: kubelet OOM, GPU driver fails, and NodeReady flapping to paging rules. Pager should include region, nodepool name, and last applied kubelet flags.

alex: handoff checklist (short):
- control plane kubeadm join token rotated and persisted
- CNI running and MTU validated
- GPU driver + device-plugin running on every GPU node
- node labels & taints applied
- base addons healthy (coredns, metrics-server, kube-proxy)
- smoke tests passed (dns, gpu, network)
- autoscaler policies pushed to infra-apiserver
- cost runbook and expected utilization numbers documented
- oncall playbook and runbook link: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/ap-south3-kubeadm-priming

maya: can you add a short rollback plan?

alex: rollback: scale GPU nodepool down to zero, drain nodes, revert CNI config to previous stable, re-image nodes with last known-good AMI, reapply device-plugin if missing. If control-plane bad: restore etcd snapshot (link in runbook) and re-run kubeadm restore.

aaron: quick Q: who signs off before we flip traffic?

alex: signoff from infra lead (maya) + SRE oncall + cost owner (jin). After smoke tests pass and 24h stability metric: p95 pod startup < 6s, NodeReady stable no restarts.

maya: OK I'm good to own signoff. alex please leave the PR with the checklist and I'll approve in the morning. :thumbsup:

alex: will do. leaving step-by-step commands in the PR and linking to runbook. tagging @oncall once PR merged.

ops-bot: PR merged: infra/ap-south3/kubeadm-priming #512 by alex at 1719877800

alex: thanks team — will post final handoff once we see the smoke tests green.

maya: thanks — bring your coffee for the 07:00 burn test. :coffee:
